archimate:Principle.name: choreography
archimate:Principle.documentation:
CONTEXT
The Integration Layer Pilot proves three patterns on Azure Integration Services. For Choreography, a change in a source system is published as an event to Azure Service Bus, and subscribing applications receive it without direct or point-to-point connections.
Dynamics 365 (Dataverse) is the master for Organisation and Customer data, so it is the source for the choreography pilot. There are multiple sources for master copy of Building data. SAHP is one of them that provides data for service bus, pending confirmation of any other sources also need to be considered.
The earlier design routed the data through the Enterprise Data Layer (EDL) and the Data Platform. The data architect meeting concluded that the EDL is a downstream reporting and analytics layer and not the operational master, and that the Data Platform is not yet mature enough to be a dependency.
Further discussions are planned with Dynamics 365 team to enable change trigger/tracking events on the relavant tables of Organisation & Customer which producer component on the service bus detects, maps and publishes them as topic for consumers.
PROPOSAL
Use Dynamics 365 to the integration layer to Service Bus. When an Organisation or Customer record changes, a trigger in Dynamics 365 calls an API in the integration layer, hosted on AKS. The API maps the data to the canonical Organisation and Customer models and publishes it as an event to a Service Bus topic. Subscribers receive events through their own subscriptions. The EDL is removed from the flow and may subscribe later like any other consumer.
Building events from SAHP can follow the same pattern once the source is confirmed.
Why this option - Dynamics holds the master copy of Organisation and Customer data, so changes are published from the source of truth. - The trigger sends changes as they happen, so subscribers get events without delay and no polling is needed. - Follows the HLD principles and avoids dependence on undecided Data Platform scope.
Options not proposed - Option 2, Dynamics to Data Platform (EDL) to Service Bus: makes the pilot depend on undecided Data Platform scope.
Consequences - The integration layer owns the API, mapping and publishing, which adds build effort. - The CRM team needs to configure the trigger in Dynamics and agree how it authenticates to the API. - If the API is unavailable when Dynamics calls it, the change could be missed, so retry and failure handling must be agreed/discussed.
Open points - Confirm the Building data source (SAHP). - Obtain the canonical Organisation, Customer and Building models. - Confirm Dynamics trigger configuration and access for each environment.
Status: Proposed
